Bug_Title: "Object.wait()", "Object.notify()" and "Object.notifyAll()" should only be called from synchronized code
Bug_Details:
The Object.wait(…​) , Object.notify() and Object.notifyAll() methods are used in multithreaded environments
to coordinate interdependent tasks that are performed by different threads. These methods are not thread-safe and by contract, they require the
invoking Thread to own the object’s monitor. If a thread invokes one of these methods without owning the object’s monitor an IllegalMonitorStateException is thrown.
Bug_Explanation: The methods Object.wait() and Object.notify() are called outside of a synchronized block. The thread invoking these methods must own the object's monitor, otherwise an IllegalMonitorStateException is thrown.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggered the bug by calling the 'showBug' method, which contains calls to 'lock.wait()' and 'lock.notify()' outside of a synchronized block. This results in an IllegalMonitorStateException being thrown.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that the test passed successfully without any exceptions or errors, indicating that the bug was not triggered during this test run.
